card.title: SECTION II
card.flavorText: The Second department of Polish General Staff of the Polish Army, also known as Section II, was responsible for military intelligence, cryptography and analysis of foreign affairs. The department existed officially from 1918-1939, but after the German invasion of Poland almost all commanders of Section II managed to escape the country and resumed their work with French and British intelligence agencies. After the fall of France the agency worked mostly from Britain, but had an elaborate network of agents who supplied information to the Allies throughout the war which made a significant difference in the war effort. Members of Section II also developed techniques to decipher the German Enigma enciphered messages that formed the basis of the Enigma decryption that was later developed by the British at  Bletchley Park.
